prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Companion Journey", "Select the experience style that best fits your daily desktop routine.", "Journey Modes"]
1: ["Signing in links your pet safely to your cloud account so your companion state is never lost.", "Your pet stays backed up across app restarts and updates."]
2: ["Crafting Your Custom Pet", "Our engine is analyzing your photo and generating your desktop companion."]
3: ["Preview Your Companion's Spirit", "See how your pet responds and moves before completing the adoption form."]
4: ["Preparing Desktop Companion...", "Check desktop permissions if your pet is not visible immediately."]
5: ["Desktop Readiness Diagnostics", "Verifying screen overlay permissions and graphics renderer status."]
6: ["Your Companion is Live!", "Right-click your pet for actions, double-click to interact, or press Esc to hide.", "Essential Shortcuts"]
7: []
8: ["Complete Your First Bond", "Click and drag your pet across your screen to complete setup!", "Start Interacting"]
9: ["Focus mode keeps your pet quiet in the corner; Playful mode triggers periodic desk activities."]

verdicts.problem: Asks for or uses personal information (photo).
